planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; its narrow upright habit suits tight side yards and vertical accents better than spreading sasanqua types.

directions: Jessica's Ruffles is a Southern Living Plant Collection sasanqua selected for an upright, columnar habit and medium pink, semi-double blooms with ruffled petals that open from November into December. Its narrow vertical form fits foundation corners, screening rows, and other tight spaces where a typical wide-spreading camellia would not. Give it consistently moist, humus-rich, acidic soil and avoid heavy pruning except to shape right after flowering, since next year's buds set soon afterward. The flowers hold up well as cut stems, and the plant otherwise needs only an annual spring feeding and a steady mulch layer over its shallow root zone.

planting.note: Plant in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in part shade; morning sun with afternoon shade gives the best bloom without wilting the oak-shaped leaves.

directions: Tara is a Southern Living Plant Collection oakleaf hydrangea bred for dense, double white florets packed tightly into a mophead-shaped panicle, a departure from the more open conical trusses of older oakleaf cultivars. Blooms age from white through soft pink tones over the summer before the coarse, lobed foliage turns wine-red in fall, giving the shrub two separate seasons of color. It prefers the same moist, part-shade woodland-edge conditions as other oakleaf hydrangeas and should be pruned only right after flowering, since it sets next year's buds on old wood soon after. Established plants tolerate short dry spells better than bigleaf hydrangeas and need only an early spring feeding.

planting.note: Plant in spring or fall in well-drained, neutral-to-alkaline soil in full sun to part shade; good drainage is the main requirement since dianthus crowns rot quickly in soggy winter soil.

directions: Blueberry Pie is a Southern Living Plant Collection dianthus in the American Pie series, producing hot pink blooms with a contrasting lavender-pink eye on compact, evergreen mounds from spring through fall. Its extended, heat-tolerant bloom season carries it through Gulf South summers better than older spring-only dianthus strains, and spent flowers can simply be sheared back lightly to push another flush. It draws butterflies and hummingbirds and holds up well as a cut flower. Give it sharp drainage and full sun for the tightest habit and heaviest bloom; part shade is tolerated but flowering slows.

planting.note: Set out after all frost danger in full sun in average, well-drained soil; grown almost entirely for its season-long carmine-red foliage rather than its sparse, infrequent maroon flowers.

directions: Panama Red is a Southern Living Plant Collection selection of cranberry hibiscus grown as a bold foliage accent, holding its rich, deeply lobed carmine-red leaves through peak summer heat without fading to bronze the way many older red-leaf hibiscus do. It flowers only sparingly, so the real display is the dense color mass of the foliage itself, which works well as a thriller in large containers or a hot-colored summer hedge. Treat it as a tender perennial outside zone 9 and up, cutting it back hard and mulching heavily if attempting to overwinter it farther north, or simply root fresh cuttings indoors over winter the way coleus is handled.

planting.note: Plant in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to part shade; its dense, naturally tidy habit needs little corrective pruning.

directions: Stellar Ruby is a Southern Living Plant Collection banana shrub selected for pink-to-ruby-hued flowers with the classic sweet, banana-like fragrance of the species, opening over a long window from late spring through summer and sporadically into early fall rather than the single spring flush of the common green-flowered form. Its dense evergreen habit and moderate size make it useful as a fragrant screen or specimen near a patio or window where the scent can be enjoyed up close. It is otherwise grown exactly like other banana shrubs, tolerating heat and humidity well and needing only light shaping after the main bloom period.

planting.note: Plant in fall or spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun for the best gold variegation; tolerates poor, sandy, or salt-affected coastal soil once established.

directions: Olive Martini is a Southern Living Plant Collection evergreen Elaeagnus grown for its olive-green leaves edged in gold, with silvery new growth that adds a third tone as it emerges through the season. It makes a fast, dense privacy screen or informal hedge and shrugs off heat, drought, salt spray, and poor soil better than most broadleaf evergreens of similar size, making it a strong fit for exposed Gulf Coast sites. Give it full sun for the strongest variegation, since shaded plants tend to green up and lose contrast, and prune after its inconspicuous but fragrant fall flowers to control size on what is otherwise a vigorous, fast-growing shrub.

planting.note: Plant in spring in full sun and lean, well-drained soil; good drainage matters more than soil fertility, since rich, wet soil shortens the plant's life.

directions: Celebration is part of the REALFLOR Sunset series of blanket flower, bred for rich red, fade-resistant petals over dark pink-and-yellow centers on a compact, floriferous mound that blooms nearly year-round in mild climates rather than pausing through midsummer heat the way older gaillardia strains do. It needs no deadheading to keep reblooming, though trimming spent flower heads tidies the plant and can encourage an even heavier flush. As with other blanket flowers it thrives on neglect, wanting lean, sharply drained soil, full sun, and minimal supplemental water once established, making it a dependable, low-input filler for hot, dry Gulf Coast borders and pollinator beds.

planting.note: Plant in fall or spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; its naturally tight mound needs little to no shearing to stay neat.

directions: Mini Touch is a dwarf Japanese holly bred as a tidy, low-maintenance stand-in for boxwood, holding a dense, rounded 2-by-2-foot mound of tiny, dark green, boxwood-like leaves without the boxwood blight and leafminer problems that plague true Buxus in hot, humid climates. Its fine texture and naturally neat habit suit low edging, foundation plantings, and container work with little to no shearing required to keep its shape. It tolerates full sun to part shade and average garden soil, and like other Ilex crenata selections appreciates a consistent watering schedule while it establishes a root system.

scientific_name: Philadelphus lewisii x coronarius 'G15097' (Pearls of Perfume) PP32770

planting.note: Plant in fall or spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; deadheading spent clusters encourages continued rebloom through the season.

directions: Pearls of Perfume is a compact mock orange hybrid bred to rebloom in flushes from spring through fall rather than flowering only in a single brief spring burst like most mock orange shrubs, while keeping the double white, citrus-scented blooms the genus is known for. Its smaller, more restrained frame fits a mixed shrub border or foundation planting better than older, larger-growing mock orange species. Plant it where the fragrance can be appreciated near a walkway, patio, or open window, and prune lightly right after each bloom flush to tidy the shrub without sacrificing the next round of flowers.

planting.note: Plant in fall or spring in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; good air movement around the dense canopy helps limit the leaf-spot problems common to Indian hawthorn.

directions: Spring Sonata is a Southern Living Plant Collection Indian hawthorn in the Clean Sweep disease-resistant line, bred for improved resistance to the leaf-spot fungus that disfigures older Rhaphiolepis cultivars in humid Gulf Coast summers. It carries clean white flower clusters each spring on a dense, glossy-leaved mound, followed by dark purple berries that persist into winter and add food value for birds. Its salt tolerance makes it a reliable choice for coastal and seaside plantings, and it otherwise needs only an occasional light shaping, since it holds a naturally rounded form without heavy pruning.
